verdict.reasoning: Patient reports 'aching all over' and 'feeling really tired, run down' for 'definitely the last six weeks'.
Patient states symptoms started 'probably a couple of weeks after I got back' from a holiday that 'probably coincided... End of January, start of Feb.'
Patient says 'I do quite a lot of walking, and we did, quite a lot while we were out... I was in shorts and, and boots' and 'I don't recall any bugs, I don't remember seeing anything bitten.'
When asked about weight: 'I don't think so... I'm probably less hungry, but no, no weight change.'
Patient says 'I've been going to work. I don't know how effective it's been' and 'Not as much... I'm not exercising as I would normally.'

Patient describes rash 'sort of calf, back of my calf' first noticed 'around the end of February, the middle to end of Feb' that 'faded over a couple of weeks' and 'didn't actually cause too much itching.'
Patient: 'it turns out it was a bit of a sore throat I had... so possibly a little bit feverish.' This was discussed in context of the rash timing.
In response to 'Any persistent cold symptoms or earaches, sore throat, chest cough, shortness of breath, phlegm, anything like that?' patient answers 'Uh, no.'
Same question includes 'chest cough, shortness of breath, phlegm' and patient responds 'Uh, no.'
To 'Any difficulty swallowing or acid in your throat, or abdominal pain?' patient answers 'No.'
To 'Any change in your bowel habit, diarrhoea, vomiting or blood in the stool?' patient replies 'Uh, no.'
To 'Any difficulty passing urine or blood in the urine?' patient replies 'No, that's all fine.'
To 'any headaches, blurred vision, tingling, numbness?' patient reports only general headache/malaise and denies tingling or numbness, indicating no focal neurological symptoms.
Doctor asks about 'swelling of your joints' and specifically 'Your hands, wrists, ankles, toes.' Patient responds 'No.'
Patient mentions 'the sort of headache maybe in just generally feeling a bit crappy,' indicating occasional headache with malaise.
When asked about significant past medical problems, patient states 'Asthma... if they can help.'
Same response includes 'Asthma and hay fever if they can help.'
Patient: 'I've got one of those, um, preventative, I think... I've been using the everyday for the morning and night.'
Patient: 'I take, um, one of the antihistamines... I get that from, just from the pharmacy,' indicating over-the-counter use.
Patient says 'I work for a health technology company actually' and later 'just my wife' when asked who he lives with.
On alcohol: Doctor asks 'Drink any alcohol?' Patient clarifies 'Sorry, occasionally.'
Summary matches: fatigue and aching 'for the last six weeks' after travel; 'aching shoulders, back, the hips, knees'; and a calf rash 'middle to end of Feb' that resolved over 'a couple of weeks.'
Doctor explains need to check 'a bacterial infection... called lyme disease' and also 'other things... which can cause reduced energy, tiredness and aching for, persistent over six weeks.'

Doctor: 'get some blood tests, checking all the normal things, like liver, kidneys, blood count, etc. But also... one which you can get which can produce a rash like that' referring to Lyme; FBC/U&E/LFT are standard interpretations of 'blood count, liver, kidneys.'
Doctor: 'if that comes back positive, then there are specific antibiotics that we would give you to treat it,' referring to Lyme disease testing.
Doctor: 'if you book that through the support line, and then when you've had the test arrange a follow up about a week after... we can do that over the phone.'
Patient: 'there was, uh, in fact I've got a photo, um, on my phone... I can try and show you' of the rash; doctor responds 'OK, right, yeah,' indicating review of prior photo.
